At 5% simple interest on Rs 10000 the interest is a flat Rs 500 a year, so the balance after t completed years is 10000 + 500t. The key reads "in the 15th year" as the balance STANDING DURING year 15, i.e. after 14 completed years: 10000 + 14(500) = 17000. Our solution read it as the balance at the END of year 15: 10000 + 15(500) = 17500 — which is the amount during the 16th year. The key is internally consistent under one clock: "in the kth year" = 10000 + 500(k-1) gives 17000 at k = 15, while "after 20 years" = 10000 + 500(20) gives 20000, and both of its printed figures follow from that single model. Equivalently, on the standard end-of-year A.P. 10500, 11000, 11500, ... (a = 10500, d = 500) the amount during the 15th year is the 14th term, 10500 + 13(500) = 17000. The key's reading is the standard textbook one and is the more literal reading of "in" versus "after", so it is adopted.
